To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we formally study the problem of spurious correlation, and our analysis naturally offers solutions to it.

(i) we can bound the generalization error of a learning problem when there exist features that are associated with the labels only in the training distribution; (ii) our bound can be tight; (iii) our bound can suggest a solution to the problem; (iv) the solution does not require any domain knowledge.

(1) the generalization error can be bounded by the difference between the training distribution and the testing distribution; (2) the error bound can be further bounded by how spurious the features are; (3) this error bound can be tighter than the domain adaptation error bound, and (4) there are solutions that can be applied to this problem, and these solutions are all linked to established solutions for other robustness problems.
